title: A quantitative and non-invasive method for nanoparticle translocation and toxicity evaluation in a human airway barrier model
author: Zhang, Aquino, et al.
materials: Maintain the cultures following provider's instruction in proper media under appropriate culture conditions until the desired confluence. Standard culture conditions for above mentioned cells are 37 °C, humid air mixture containing 5% CO2.1.2The three selected cell types in the co-culture model each require its own type of media. Prepare and store all media in sterile conditions, and use them in biological safety cabinets only. Product details (such as vendor and catalog number) are summarized in the material list spreadsheet in the supporting information.1.2.1All media are prepared with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) and 1% penicillin-streptomycin (PS) supplement. Store FBS and PS routinely in −20 °C. Before use, thaw heat-inactivated FBS and PS aliquots in water bath at 37 °C.1.2.2Make medium for endothelial EA.hy926 cells.1.2.2.1First combine Dulbecco's Modified Eagle's Medium (DMEM) powder formula, 1.5 g of sodium bicarbonate, 0.11 g sodium pyruvate, 4.5 g d-glucose, 2 vials of l-glutamine (0.292 g per vial), 15.9 mg phenol red and thawed 10 mL PS with 900 ml nanopure water (18.2 Ω-cm purity) in a 1000 mL graduated cylinder.1.2.2.2Adjust medium pH level to 7.25 with 1 M hydrochloric acid (HCl) or 1 M Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) solutions, before adding 100 mL of thawed FBS.1.2.2.3Stir well, and filter the 1000 mL medium through a 0.2 µm sterile filter into sterile medium container. This medium is referred as DMEM-high, due to its higher glucose level compared to regular DMEM formula.1.2.3Make medium for epithelial Calu-3 cells.1.2.3.1Similarly, combine DMEM powder formula, 1.5 g of sodium bicarbonate, 0.11 g sodium pyruvate, 1.5 g d-glucose, 1 vial of l-glutamine (0.292 g), 15.9 mg phenol red and thawed 10 mL PS with 900 mL nanopure water in a 1000 mL graduated cylinder.1.2.3.2After adjusting medium pH level to 7.25, add 100 mL thawed FBS to the cylinder.1.2.3.3Filter the 1000 mL medium through a 0.2 µm sterile filter after thorough mixing. This medium is referred as DMEM-low because of the relative low glucose level.1.2.4Make medium for monocytic leukemia Thp-1 cells.1.2.4.1Prepare Roswell Park Memorial Institute (RPMI) 1640 medium by combining RPMI 1640 medium powder formula, 1.5 g sodium bicarbonate, 0.11 g sodium pyruvate, 4.5 g d-glucose, 2.383 g 4-(2-hydroxyethyl)−1-piperazineethanesolfonic acid (HEPES), 15.9 mg phenol red and thawed 10 mL PS in 900 mL nanopure water.1.2.4.2Adjust its pH to 7.25 with HCl and NaOH, and supplemented with 100 mL thawed FBS before filtering through a 0.2 µm sterile filter into storage container.1.2.5Store all media at 4 °C, and warm to 37 °C prior to use on cells in sterile environment.2Co-culture model2.1The complete air-blood barrier is built upon a mature bi-culture of epithelial and endothelial cells (Fig. 1).2.1.1First, build the bi-culture of EA.hy926 and Calu-3 by growing them on the opposite sides of a 1.0 µm pore size membrane insert. steps.title: Prepare cell culture media
steps.instruction: Make three sterile media each containing 10 % FBS and 1 % penicillin‑streptomycin (PS). Thaw heat‑inactivated FBS and PS at 37 °C before use.

substeps.instruction: Endothelial (EA.hy926) medium (DMEM‑high): dissolve DMEM powder, add 1.5 g NaHCO₃, 0.11 g Na‑pyruvate, 4.5 g d‑glucose, 2 vials l‑glutamine (0.292 g each), 15.9 mg phenol red, and 10 mL thawed PS in 900 mL nanopure water (18.2 Ω·cm). Adjust pH to 7.25 with 1 M HCl or NaOH, add 100 mL thawed FBS, stir, filter through 0.2 µm filter into sterile container.
Epithelial (Calu‑3) medium (DMEM‑low): same as above but use 1.5 g d‑glucose and 1 vial l‑glutamine. Adjust pH to 7.25, add 100 mL FBS, mix, filter (0.2 µm).

Monocytic (Thp‑1) medium (RPMI‑1640): dissolve RPMI‑1640 powder, add 1.5 g NaHCO₃, 0.11 g Na‑pyruvate, 4.5 g d‑glucose, 2.383 g HEPES, 15.9 mg phenol red, 10 mL thawed PS in 900 mL water. Adjust pH to 7.25, add 100 mL FBS, filter (0.2 µm).

steps.title: Warm and store media
steps.instruction: Store all prepared media at 4 °C; warm to 37 °C in a sterile environment immediately before use.

steps.title: Assemble endothelial‑epithelial bi‑culture
steps.instruction: Grow EA.hy926 and Calu‑3 on opposite sides of a 1.0 µm polyester membrane insert in a 12‑well plate.

substeps.instruction: Invert inserts in a 100 × 21 mm petri dish (up to 6 inserts per dish).
Seed 200 µL EA.hy926 suspension (2.5 × 10⁴ cells/cm²) onto the basolateral side; incubate 2 h for attachment.
Aspirate excess medium gently, rinse basolateral surface twice with fresh medium.
Flip inserts, place into receiving wells of a 12‑well plate, add 1.5 mL DMEM‑high to each well.
Seed 500 µL Calu‑3 suspension (5.0 × 10⁴ cells/cm²) onto the apical side; incubate ~4 h (≈50 % attachment) in DMEM‑low.
Replace medium in both compartments every other day (1.5 mL basal, 0.5 mL apical).

steps.title: Monitor TEER until barrier formed
steps.instruction: Measure transepithelial electrical resistance (TEER) daily; proceed when TEER exceeds 1000 Ω·cm².

steps.title: Add and differentiate Thp‑1 macrophages
steps.instruction: Introduce Thp‑1 cells into the mature bi‑culture and induce differentiation with PMA.

substeps.instruction: When TEER > 1000 Ω·cm², remove apical medium and add mixed medium (DMEM‑low : RPMI‑1640 = 5:1) containing 2.0 × 10⁴ Thp‑1 cells.
Add phorbol 12‑myristate 13‑acetate (PMA) to a final concentration of 100 ng/mL; incubate 48 h at 37 °C.
Discard PMA‑containing medium, replace with fresh mixed medium.
Rest cultures an additional 48 h to allow macrophage‑like attachment; TEER will drop then recover.
Continue daily TEER monitoring until it again exceeds 1000 Ω·cm², indicating a stable triple‑culture barrier.

steps.title: Measure TEER of barrier
steps.instruction: Determine barrier resistance using a Voltohmmeter with STX2 electrodes.

substeps.instruction: Sanitize electrodes in 70 % ethanol, then rinse in culture medium.
Place a cell‑free insert in 1.5 mL DMEM‑high (basal) and 0.5 mL DMEM‑low (apical) to obtain background resistance TEER₀.
Insert the short electrode into the apical chamber and the long electrode into the basal well (touching the bottom); read TEER₀.
Repeat the procedure with the cultured insert to obtain TEERe.
Calculate TEER = (TEERe – TEER₀) × A, where A = 1.12 cm² (membrane area).
Take three readings per insert, average them, and compare to the 1000 Ω·cm² benchmark.

steps.title: Expose barrier to AgNPs
steps.instruction: Treat the triple‑culture with silver nanoparticles for 24 h.

substeps.instruction: Prepare AgNP stock (1 mg/mL, sterile, endotoxin‑free).
Add 1.5 µL of stock to the apical chamber (0.5 mL mixed medium) to achieve a final concentration of 3 mg/L.
Return the plate to the 37 °C incubator for 24 h.

steps.title: Collect samples for uptake analysis
steps.instruction: Harvest media, rinses, and cells from both compartments after nanoparticle exposure.

substeps.instruction: A) Collect ~0.5 mL apical medium (sample A).
B) Collect ~1.5 mL basal medium (sample B).
C) Rinse apical side with 1 mL PBS three times; combine rinses with sample A.
D) Rinse basolateral side and receiving well with 1 mL PBS three times; combine rinses with sample B.
E) Add 0.25 mL Trypsin‑EDTA (0.25 %/0.53 mM) to the insert and 1 mL to the well; incubate 3 min at 37 °C.
F) Aspirate detached cells from apical side (sample C) and from basolateral side (sample D).
G) Rinse membrane both sides with PBS and add the washes to their respective cellular samples (C and D).

steps.title: Digest samples for ICP‑MS
steps.instruction: Prepare all collected samples for silver quantification by ICP‑MS.

substeps.instruction: Add 3 mL concentrated HNO₃ (67–70 %) and Rhodium standard solution (1000 µg/mL) to each sample.
Heat‑digest at 105 °C for 6 h.
Dilute each digested sample five‑fold with nanopure water to obtain a final Rh concentration of 10 mg/L.
Run ICP‑MS using calibration standards prepared in 2 % HNO₃ containing 10 mg/L Rh; standards at 0, 1, 10, 25, 50, 100 mg/L Ag.
Include quality‑control samples (e.g., 1 and 10 mg/L Ag) between experimental runs.

steps.title: Prepare LDH assay reagents
steps.instruction: Make fresh LDH detection solution for cytotoxicity measurement.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 200 mM Tris (pH 8.0): dissolve 2.222 g Tris‑HCl and 1.06 g Tris‑base in 100 mL nanopure water (100 mL batch).
Prepare 50 mM Li lactate: dissolve 1.96 g lithium lactate in 100 mL water (100 mL batch).
Make 33 mg/mL INT: dissolve 330 mg INT in 10 mL DMSO.
Make 9 mg/mL PMS: dissolve 90 mg PMS in 10 mL nanopure water.
Make 3.74 mg/mL NAD: dissolve 0.344 g NAD in 92 mL nanopure water.
Combine 200 µL INT, 200 µL PMS, and 4.6 mL NAD to obtain a 5 mL INT/PMS/NAD mixture (prepare fresh, darken over time).
Mix 5 mL Tris, 5 mL Li lactate, and 5 mL INT/PMS/NAD mixture to obtain the complete LDH assay reagent (sufficient for 100 tests in a 96‑well plate).

steps.title: Collect pre‑treatment conditioned medium
steps.instruction: Before adding AgNPs, aspirate and store the spent medium from the apical insert and the basal well separately as control samples.

steps.title: Collect post‑treatment media
steps.instruction: After the 24‑h AgNP exposure, aspirate the medium from the insert (apical) and from the receiving well (basal) and keep them separate for LDH analysis.

steps.title: Perform LDH cytotoxicity assay
steps.instruction: Quantify extracellular LDH released from cells using the prepared reagents.

substeps.instruction: For each sample (control or treated), mix 1 mL conditioned medium with 3 mL LDH assay reagent in a tube.
Transfer 200 µL of the mixture into each well of a clean 96‑well plate; use at least 8 replicates per condition.
Incubate protected from light for 5 min.
Measure absorbance at 490 nm with a microplate reader.

steps.title: Analyze LDH data
steps.instruction: Calculate LDH leakage relative to spontaneous release and optionally as percent of maximal release.

substeps.instruction: Baseline (spontaneous) LDH = average absorbance of control wells.
Induced LDH = average absorbance of treated wells minus baseline.
Optional: Determine maximal LDH by lysing identical cell numbers with 1 % Triton X; compute % max leakage = (observed LDH / maximal LDH) × 100 %.
Apply appropriate statistical tests to compare groups.
